--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.prize_collecting_steiner_tree()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Find a prize-collecting Steiner tree. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.prize_collecting_steiner_tree()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Find a prize-collecting Steiner tree. title: >- [Graph.prize_collecting_steiner_tree()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Find a prize-collecting Steiner tree. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Find a prize-collecting Steiner tree. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L86375-L86491){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.prize_collecting_steiner_tree( prizes, edge_penalty=1.0, weight_attr=None, return_subgraph=True, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Prize-collecting Steiner tree](../assets/graphs/prize-collecting-steiner-tree.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The weighted graph from the steiner_tree figure, with a prize p in a badge on nodes A (1), B (5), C (5), and E (4); edge weights are costs. The tree B–D, D–C, D–E (accent) collects B, C, and E through the prize-less node D, while A is left out and faded because its prize of 1 does not pay for any edge costing 3. The card lists the tree edges and its prize 14 against cost 5." width="100%"} A variant of the Steiner tree where each node has a *prize* (benefit of inclusion) and each edge has a *cost* (penalty for inclusion). The algorithm finds a connected subtree that maximizes total prize minus total edge cost. Unlike the standard Steiner tree, not all prize nodes need to be included if the cost of connecting them is too high. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [prizes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict[int | str, float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Dictionary mapping nodes (integer IDs or string labels) to prize values (e.g., `-log10(p_value)` from GWAS hits). Only nodes with prizes are candidates for inclusion. [edge_penalty]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Multiplier applied to edge weights as costs. Higher values penalize longer paths more aggressively, producing smaller trees. Default `1.0`. [weight_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Edge attribute to use for weights. If `None` or `"weight"`, uses the edge's weight field. Under any other name, every edge must hold a number. [return_subgraph]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), returns a new Graph with the tree's nodes and edges, keeping their IDs, labels, weights and attributes. If `False`, returns `(source_id, target_id, weight)` edge tuples. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph or list[tuple[int, int, float]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The prize-collecting Steiner tree as a graph or edge list. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If any prize node doesn't exist in the graph, or `weight_attr=` names an attribute that an edge lacks or holds as a non-number. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~steiner_tree`) : The cheapest tree that connects every one of a set of nodes. [](`~expand_seed_set`) : Grow a module from seeds by how tightly candidates link to it. ## Examples {.doc-examples} `BRCA1`, `TP53` and `CHEK2` carry prizes. The tree collects all three, since each prize is worth more than the edges that reach it, and passes through the prize-less `ATM`. `MDM2` has no prize, so it is left out: ::: {#34003621 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph.from_edges( [("BRCA1", "ATM", 1.0), ("ATM", "CHEK2", 1.0), ("ATM", "TP53", 2.0), ("TP53", "MDM2", 1.0)] ) tree = graph.prize_collecting_steiner_tree({"BRCA1": 5.0, "TP53": 3.0, "CHEK2": 4.0}) tree.get_edges_str_repr(use_labels=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['BRCA1--ATM', 'ATM--CHEK2', 'ATM--TP53'] ``` ::: ::: ### Connecting disease genes `proteins()` is a small protein interaction network with five known disease genes. With a prize of `3` for each disease gene and a cost of `1` for each edge, the tree links four of them through REP3, collecting `12` for a cost of `4`: ::: {#31853370 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} proteins = ec.proteins() disease = ["REP1", "REP2", "REP5", "CYC2", "TRN3"] tree = proteins.prize_collecting_steiner_tree({gene: 3.0 for gene in disease}) tree.get_edges_str_repr(use_labels=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ['REP1--REP2', 'REP1--REP3', 'REP3--REP5', 'REP5--CYC2'] ``` ::: ::: TRN3, on the far side of the network, is left out: it is three edges from the rest, and reaching it would cost as much as its prize: ::: {#d7826353 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} proteins.plot( layout="pos", highlight={"accent": disease}, highlight_edges={"soft": tree.get_edge_ids()}, label_by="label", ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: Halving the cost of an edge with `edge_penalty=0.5` makes TRN3 worth reaching, through the chaperone HSP1 and TRN2: ::: {#a5879c66 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} tree = proteins.prize_collecting_steiner_tree( {gene: 3.0 for gene in disease}, edge_penalty=0.5 ) proteins.plot( layout="pos", highlight={"accent": disease}, highlight_edges={"soft": tree.get_edge_ids()}, label_by="label", ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: [Network biology](../user-guide/network-biology.qmd#connecting-high-scoring-genes) connects high-scoring genes on a larger simulated network.
